A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AEGIS framework, dataset and diagnostic-learning experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFT, GRPO and DCL experiments on Aegis-Bench and Who&When, including benchmark results, ablations and training analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains those experiments and adds original human label validation, distributional comparisons, additional results and a failure case study.

M1.justification: The pipeline and three learning approaches remain. However, Section 5.2 removes v1's requirement that the predicted agent be outside the ground-truth agent set before receiving partial error credit. This changes the stated reward rule in some cases. The expanded DCL walkthrough primarily documents existing components.

E1.justification: The six source benchmarks, six MAS frameworks and Who&When evaluation remain. v5 additionally uses MAST-Data trajectories in its distributional realism analysis (Appendix B.3), providing a limited extension of empirical data coverage. The additional Who&When case comes from an already evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator models and ablations. v5 Table 10 adds a +hard-neg DCL variant to the ablation comparison. Its new geographic case also compares AEGIS with Claude-Sonnet-4, o3 and Gemini-2.5-Pro, extending the qualitative comparisons beyond v1's financial case.

E3.justification: v5 adds distinct evaluation designs: a blinded audit of 100 trajectories by three experts, and a distributional comparison using cleaned trajectories, all-MiniLM-L6-V2 embeddings, silhouette scores and centroid distances. It also adds precision/recall metrics and cross-model correlation analysis. The original benchmark splits and reported training budgets remain.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining v1's CoT, training-epoch, architecture and DCL analyses, v5 adds label-fidelity validation, synthetic-versus-real distributional analysis, cross-benchmark correlations and a hard-negative ablation. Appendix A.2 adds a geographic case where AEGIS and all displayed comparators miss the root cause, substantially broadening the investigation of reliability and failure conditions.

E5.justification: v1 already reports three DCL seeds and states a mean/standard-deviation reporting practice, but v5 first supplies the actual per-metric standard deviations in Table 10. It also adds human/program agreement statistics and Pearson correlation p-values. These expand statistical reporting without establishing an increase in the existing DCL run count.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical entries remain unchanged, including Aegis-SFT's 26.51 average. v5 adds precision and recall tables, hard-negative results, agreement scores of 0.85 and 0.81, distributional measurements, cross-benchmark correlations and the all-model failure case. These substantially expand reported outcomes rather than demonstrate improved performance for the retained main experiments.

T1.justification: Removing the agent-set restriction from the partial-error reward changes a formal definition in Section 5.2. Otherwise, the attribution-map reformulation is equivalent, and the DCL loss equations are retained in Appendix C. The added standard SFT/GRPO exposition does not introduce new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about automated synthesis, three learning paradigms, competitive diagnostic performance and transfer remain. v5 removes the Introduction's specific claim that the dataset is two orders of magnitude larger than prior resources, retaining the less specific claim that it is substantially larger.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive qualifications concerning SFT over-specialization on underrepresented MAS, subtle numerical failures and taxonomy/injection limitations. It introduces JSON parsing failures as an explanation for CoT degradation and corrects Figure 4's interpretation from error classes to k-means clusters. New discussions also interpret label agreement, distributional realism and uneven cross-benchmark correlations.

D1.justification: Appendices B–E substantially expand documentation of task evaluators, response-token masking, GRPO optimization, DCL pair construction and parameter counts. They disclose a 32,768-token evaluation limit and provide GAIA judging and Who&When classification prompts. This does not establish changed settings for the retained experiments. Conversely, v1's explicit project-website link is absent from v5.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations for supervised contrastive learning, AutoEnv and the Claude/o3 system cards, and replaces the general Maron–Lozano-Pérez MIL citation with Ilse et al.'s attention-based MIL work. The broader positioning around MAS failures and automated data synthesis remains stable.

P1.justification: v5 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and results discussion, consistently changes identification terminology to attribution, and condenses the contribution list. It reorganizes v1's single appendix hierarchy into Appendices A–E and moves detailed loss exposition out of the main text. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: v5 adds the geographic case and distribution plots (Figures 6–7), six tables covering validation, parameters and supplementary results, and Algorithm 1. Existing figures and training tables are retained but relocated, with caption and label refinements and revised conference-page formatting.

improvement.justification: The blinded label audit addresses v1's lack of independent fidelity validation, while the failure case and technical documentation improve scrutiny. However, the new precision/recall tables introduce an unexplained inconsistency: Aegis-SFT's Aegis-Bench Agent micro-precision of 92.84 and micro-recall of 55.43 imply F1 about 69.42, versus 76.53 in retained Table 1. The PDFs do not reconcile these values, leaving the net effect on evidential reliability and overall quality uncertain.
